package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as ELF binaries and shell scripts, not via a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all versions as it is not a package in the traditional sense)
package_info.why_malicious: Shikitega is a multi-stage Linux malware that delivers a Metasploit meterpreter for remote control, exploits privilege escalation vulnerabilities, establishes persistence, and installs a cryptominer. It uses polymorphic encoding to evade detection and abuses legitimate cloud services for C2. Its entire purpose is malicious, providing attackers with full remote access, persistence, and illicit cryptomining capabilities.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Polymorphically encoded shellcode that downloads and executes the Metasploit 'Mettle' meterpreter payload from a remote C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code decodes itself in memory, downloads the Metasploit meterpreter payload from a remote C2 server, writes it to disk, and executes it, granting remote shell access to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-decoding shellcode that downloads and executes a remote payload is a hallmark of malware loaders.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal binaries do not contain polymorphic shellcode that fetches and executes remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Polymorphic encoding is sometimes used in security research or CTFs, but not in production software.

execution_context.file_location: meterpreter payload (downloaded and executed by dropper)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Metasploit 'Mettle' meterpreter binary, which provides a remote shell and command execution capabilities.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After being executed by the dropper, the meterpreter establishes a reverse shell to the attacker's C2 server, allowing full remote control of the infected system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Meterpreter is a well-known post-exploitation tool used by attackers for remote control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not install or execute remote access trojans.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testers may use meterpreter in authorized red team engagements.

execution_context.file_location: exploit modules within the dropper or downloaded components

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Exploit code targeting CVE-2021-3493 (overlayfs privilege escalation) and CVE-2021-4034 (Polkit pkexec privilege escalation) to gain root access.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial access, the malware executes local privilege escalation exploits to obtain root privileges, enabling further persistence and payload installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated exploitation of local vulnerabilities for privilege escalation is a common malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not exploit local vulnerabilities to gain root.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may test for vulnerabilities, but do not exploit them for persistence.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining root, the malware writes a cron job to /etc/crontab to execute the cryptominer every minute, ensuring persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses cron jobs for persistence, especially for cryptominers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely installs persistent cron jobs as root without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use cron for scheduled tasks, but not for hidden cryptominer execution.

execution_context.file_location: downloaded cryptominer binary (location set by cron job)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downloaded and executed XMRig or similar Monero cryptominer binary.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The cron job executes the cryptominer, which connects to a mining pool and uses system resources to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited cryptominer installation and execution is a clear sign of compromise.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not install or run cryptominers without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cryptomining is legitimate only when explicitly installed and configured by the system owner.

execution_context.file_location: all malware components (dropper, shell scripts, binaries)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Polymorphic encoder/obfuscator applied to all malware modules, changing the binary signature on each infection.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At every stage, the malware uses a polymorphic encoder to obfuscate its code, making static detection by antivirus engines more difficult.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Polymorphic encoding is a classic malware evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not self-modify or obfuscate its code in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for DRM or intellectual property protection, but not for malware delivery.

attack_chain.action: Initial execution of the Shikitega dropper, which uses polymorphic encoding to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of the meterpreter payload

attack_chain.action: Download and execution of the Metasploit meterpreter, providing remote shell access.
Exploit local Linux vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-3493, CVE-2021-4034) to escalate privileges to root.
Establish persistence by writing a cron job as root to execute the cryptominer.
Download and execute the cryptominer, which connects to a mining pool and uses system resources.

behavioral_signatures: Initial payload downloads and executes remote code (meterpreter)
Automated exploitation of local privilege escalation vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-3493, CVE-2021-4034)
Unauthorized creation or modification of root cron jobs
Silent installation and execution of cryptominer binaries
file_indicators: Unknown ELF binaries with polymorphic encoding
New or modified entries in /etc/crontab or /etc/cron.*
Cryptominer binaries (e.g., XMRig) in unusual locations
network_indicators: Reverse shell connections initiated by meterpreter
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unknown or obfuscated ELF binaries executing on Linux systems, especially those that download and execute remote payloads. Watch for exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2021-3493 and CVE-2021-4034. Audit /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.* for unauthorized entries, particularly those running unknown binaries as root. Detect outbound connections to known C2 domains (dash.cloudflare.ovh, main.cloudfronts.net) and mining pools. Use file integrity monitoring to detect new or modified binaries and scripts with known malicious hashes.
